name: Murky Green
lede: Murky Green is a dull, dark yellow-green named by a volunteer in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey, one of thousands of plain-English labels that survey collected.

sections.title: A crowd's plain judgment
sections.body:
Our library traces this name only to the xkcd 2010 survey; why that volunteer reached for "murky" rather than any other word is not recorded [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary's nearest block is "deep yellow green," 8.2 units from that block's centre, a loose match [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[swamp-green|Swamp Green]], 4.4 units away [2]. [[olive|Olive]] sits further out, about 5.6 units, also duller [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 48, chroma 54, hue 110 degrees, a dark, muddy green [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 46 of 23,781 paintings (22 by the within-painting lens), rarer than 60 percent of the named colors, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, found in 12 of the 8,345 paintings we have from that century, 1.3 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 22 occurrences [3]. The earliest archive match dates to 1513, 497 years before the name's 2010 record; that gap marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence the name itself is old [3]. In print, the phrase "murky green" rose fastest in the 2000s and peaked in the 2010s, tracking the survey's own timing rather than any older use [3].
